PROJECT NO. 58777


ERCOT’S MOTION FOR GOOD CAUSE EXCEPTION 
REGARDING 2027 MAGNITUDE

Electric Reliability Council of Texas, Inc. (ERCOT) files this Motion for a Good Cause Exception requesting a variance from the December 1, 2026 deadline established in 16 Texas Administrative Code (TAC) § 25.508(b)(3) in order to file the reliability standard’s magnitude update by the second quarter of 2027.  A Proposed Order that would grant this request is included as Attachment A.
Background on Reliability Standard Magnitude
The ERCOT Region’s systemwide reliability standard, established by the Public Utility Commission of Texas (Commission) in 16 TAC § 25.508, consists of three criteria: the frequency, duration, and magnitude at which a loss of load event may occur as reflected in probabilistically modeled simulations of the ERCOT System.  The values for the frequency and duration criteria are established in the rule while the magnitude criterion is updated on an annual basis.  For the magnitude criterion, § 25.508(b)(3) requires:
(3)	Magnitude.  The expected highest level of load shed during a loss of load event for the ERCOT region, measured as the average lost load for a given hour, must be less than the maximum number of megawatts of load shed that can be safely rotated during a loss of load event, as determined by ERCOT, in consultation with commission staff and the transmission operators, with a 1.00 percent exceedance tolerance.  Beginning in 2024, on or before December 1 of each year, ERCOT must file the maximum number of megawatts of load shed that can be safely rotated during a loss of load event and a summary of the methodology used to calculate this value.
To determine the magnitude criterion’s value, ERCOT has in prior years issued a Request for Information (RFI) to Transmission Operators (TOs) to determine the total megawatts (MW) in each TO’s respective load shed rotation program and, of that total, how many MW can be shed at any one time to facilitate rotation of load shed.  The aggregation of TO responses to the latter RFI question is the updated magnitude value for the ERCOT Region.  The magnitude value for 2026 is 13,988 MW based on a systemwide winter 2025-2026 peak load of 77,338 MW.
To respond to ERCOT’s RFIs, ERCOT provides the TOs with the peak load forecast for the upcoming winter, including both the total load across the ERCOT System at the peak and each TO’s respective portion of that systemwide peak load.  ERCOT has previously used the 75th percentile winter peak load forecast, excluding any load subject to curtailment under Public Utility Regulatory Act (PURA) §§ 37.0561(e) and 39.169.  
Motion for Good Cause Exception
The Commission’s rule that addresses the determination of the magnitude criterion’s value, 16 TAC § 25.508(b)(3), requires ERCOT to file by December 1 each year the maximum MW of load shed that can be safely rotated during a loss of load event and a summary of the methodology used to calculate this value.  Due to the ongoing work to finalize the Batch Zero load values, ERCOT does not yet have a final load forecast, including an official peak load forecast for winter 2026-2027.  Accordingly, ERCOT is not yet able to provide the systemwide and TO-specific total load that TOs require to respond to RFIs to provide an updated magnitude value for 2027.  For this reason, there is good cause to grant an exception to the filing deadline in 16 TAC § 25.508(b)(3).
ERCOT anticipates that the updated magnitude could be filed no later than the second quarter of 2027 after issuing RFIs near the end of the first quarter of 2027.  Pursuant to the Commission’s authority in 16 TAC § 25.3(b) to grant an exception, ERCOT respectfully requests a good cause exception to the December 1, 2026 deadline in 16 TAC § 25.508(b)(3) to instead file the magnitude value for 2027 by the second quarter of 2027.
ERCOT conferred with Commission Staff regarding its intention to seek this good cause exception and is authorized to represent that Commission Staff does not oppose this request.
Conclusion
ERCOT respectfully requests that the Commission grant ERCOT’s motion for a good cause exception to the December 1, 2026 magnitude filing deadline in 16 TAC § 25.508(b)(3) and permit ERCOT to instead file the updated magnitude value no later than the second quarter of 2027.  Granting this request will not impact reliability or day-to-day operations of the ERCOT Transmission Grid and is only necessary to ensure that more accurate information is provided to the Commission for planning purposes.  The magnitude criterion’s value is only used in assessing the long-term resource adequacy of the ERCOT Region.
ERCOT appreciates the Commission’s consideration of this motion and would be pleased to provide any additional information.  ERCOT personnel will attend the Commission’s November 19, 2026 Open Meeting to address Commissioner comments or questions.

Dated: November 6, 2026

Respectfully submitted,

PROJECT NO. 58777


PROPOSED ORDER GRANTING GOOD CAUSE EXCEPTION

On November 6, 2026, Electric Reliability Council of Texas, Inc. (ERCOT) filed with the Public Utility Commission of Texas (Commission) a motion for a good cause exception pursuant to 16 Texas Administrative Code (TAC) § 25.3(b) requesting an extension of the deadline established by 16 TAC § 25.508(b)(3), which requires ERCOT to file by December 1, 2026 the maximum number of megawatts of load shed that can be safely rotated during a loss of load event and a summary of the methodology used to calculate this value.
Under the authority established in 16 TAC § 25.3(b), the Commission grants ERCOT a good cause exception to the filing deadline established by 16 TAC § 25.508(b)(3) in order for ERCOT to instead file the updated magnitude value no later than the second quarter of 2027.  Good cause exists because the load or load forecast to be used by Transmission Operators (TOs) to provide information about their load shed rotation capabilities for magnitude determination purposes is not yet available.  After that load or load forecast becomes available, ERCOT must use that information to consult with the TOs and Commission Staff and file with the Commission as soon as practicable thereafter the maximum number of megawatts of load shed that can be safely rotated during a loss of load event and a summary of the methodology used to calculate this value.
